card.name: Purpuri
card.era: Arrived from the east early 19th c. (Oulu 1809, Helsinki 1820s); wedding centerpiece into the 1950s-60s; revived from early 1980s
card.tagline: Finland's potpourri wedding suite of sequential figure dances.
card.profile: Purpuri ('potpourri') is a suite of figure dances performed one after another, historically the principal ceremonial and social wedding dance - especially in Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnia (Kokkola, Kronoby, Nedervetil, Terjarv), western Uusimaa, Aboland and around Kaustinen (Wiki for Living Heritage; Finnish Music Quarterly). At three-day weddings, the 'rospurpuri' opened with a long polonaise ('rosa') danced by bridesmaids and groomsmen, paired by the bridal couple; later purpuris were public. It is accompanied by fiddle and by horn ensembles (e.g. Kronoby Hornkapell) when danced outdoors; the constituent dances draw on the quadrille, minuet, polska, polka and waltz.
card.insight: The purpuri was so central that the seminal Kaustinen ensemble formed in 1946 and later led by Konsta Jylha (1910-1984) was named 'Purppuripelimannit'; tradition-bearers' later adoption of national costume for staged purpuri performances entwined the dance with folk-costume display (Wiki for Living Heritage; FMQ).
card.image_significance: Finland's vast wedding-dance medley. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Finland.
